N1_SURFACE_RANKING.shape: The Scientist's proposed `rank` was adopted and improved. It lists every figure-bearing surface the manifest declares or files/ holds, plus every figure-sized raster embedded in a PDF on disk and every page worth rendering, ordered best-first by measured effective ppi, each row naming the printed size its ppi was measured against and the route to open it. Always exits 0, writes nothing anywhere, and declares in its own output what it cannot see.
N1_SURFACE_RANKING.effective_ppi_is_measured_not_assumed: Two deterministic routes: a raster whose aspect matches a PDF PAGE is a page render and its ppi is px_width / page_width_in; a raster whose aspect matches an image PLACED in a PDF takes that placement's printed width. With neither, the ppi is ASSUMED from a 7 in printed width, is printed with a `~`, and says so. On PMID 42422765 the assumption returns 104 ppi for gr7.jpg — the figure the paper's own manifest recorded by hand.
N1_SURFACE_RANKING.trap_a_vector_figure: TWO instruments, both measured, and a disagreement is reported rather than resolved. (1) Vector drawing commands on the page outside its placed rasters: 0 on each of the publisher PDF's six whole-figure pages, 0 or 1 on every text page, 365 on the figure-7 page. (2) Aspect-ratio pairing against whole-figure rasters on disk, which is the instrument that caught it in the field: the six whole-figure embedded rasters pair to 0.0001-0.0011 relative, page 11's 759x515 fragment to no closer than 0.106. When the page carries vector content, the PAGE RENDER is emitted once for that page and the fragment is demoted below it explicitly (score -1), because the fragment's own ppi is 300 and only its CONTENT is partial.
N1_SURFACE_RANKING.trap_a_flag_is_directional: An unpaired raster alone is NOT called a vector figure. A declared figure with no counterpart inside a PDF is 'no better surface on disk' — the graphical abstract ga1.jpg, 664x664, is exactly that case and a symmetric flag would have libelled it.
N1_SURFACE_RANKING.trap_b_absent_surfaces: A declared-but-absent artefact, and a raster whose container header does not parse, are kept out of the ranked list entirely and reported under `absent` with the acquisition route. Both are printed whatever the --limit, because a truncated list would drop them first.
N1_SURFACE_RANKING.acceptance_test: PASS on PMID 42422765: the top candidate is an embedded raster at 500 ppi; all six CDN JPEGs rank below it under 200 ppi; page 11 of PMC13343157.1.pdf yields exactly two candidates, the PAGE RENDER above the 759x515 fragment, with 365 vector drawings recorded; the six whole-figure pages carry 0 vector drawings and no page-render candidate.
found_by_running_it_and_fixed: ppi chosen by the LARGEST value among aspect matches reported the 400 dpi render of mmc1.pdf p.9 as 585 ppi, from a coincidental 0.0041 match in a different supplement. Now chosen by the TIGHTEST aspect gap.

a coincidental 0.0046 aspect match to an unrelated 454x274 supplement panel reported gr7.jpg at 321 ppi, three times its real resolution — lifting the very CDN raster the sub-command exists to demote. A second, stricter tolerance (MEASURE_GAP 0.002) for the ppi basis refuses it; true pairs sit at 0.0001-0.0011.
mmc2.pdf is on this corpus's disk three times byte-identical, and each of the seven CDN JPEGs twice: 504 candidates where there were 103. Now deduped by sha256 and the collapse is reported.
one PAGE RENDER was emitted per unpaired raster, printing one supplement page three times with three different nearest neighbours. Now one per page.

every page of a PDF usually shares one aspect, so a page render matched all of them and the first visited was named: the 400 dpi render of the publisher PDF's page 11 was attributed to 'mmc1.pdf p.1'. Tied bases are now collected, the ppi reported only when they agree, and the page named only when one page matches.
a 1100x90 banner strip on page 10 of PMID 29724996's article PDF ranked FIRST at 600 ppi, because the pixel bound applied to the width only. It now applies to the shorter side.

page-adjudication crops ranked first for PMID 16223882 at ~418 assumed ppi: a 2924x145 caption band is not a figure and the printed-width assumption is simply wrong for it. No ppi is claimed for a crop and it is ranked last on purpose.

N2_RETRACTION_WATCH_DECODE.reproduced_first: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x92 in position 131, from both count_rows and load_index, on a synthetic snapshot carrying one Windows-1252 right single quotation mark in a title.
N2_RETRACTION_WATCH_DECODE.call_sites_measured_not_taken: The brief named three call sites. `git grep` over the module finds TWO functions that decode the CSV — count_rows and load_index — reached from three places: build_pin (so the pin and staleness path), cmd_fetch, and every screen. Fixing the two functions fixes all three.
N2_RETRACTION_WATCH_DECODE.fix: snapshot_lines(): streams the file in binary and decodes PER PHYSICAL LINE, UTF-8 first and cp1252 on a UnicodeDecodeError. cp1252 rather than errors='replace' because it decodes every byte 0x00-0xFF (so it can never raise) and recovers the actual character instead of substituting U+FFFD into a title that is passed verbatim into a manifest block. Per line rather than per file so a snapshot that is valid UTF-8 apart from some rows stays UTF-8 for the rest, and a genuine UTF-8 multi-byte character on a clean line is never mangled into two cp1252 characters. Each yielded line keeps its terminator, so csv.reader still handles a newline inside a quoted field.
N2_RETRACTION_WATCH_DECODE.second_defect_found_and_fixed: `fetch` then `pin` — the sequence cmd_fetch's own output recommends — re-pinned the snapshot ALREADY named by the pin, because snapshot_path(read_pin()) prefers the pinned filename whenever it is still present. Measured with a 2026-09-10 and a 2026-10-02 snapshot both on disk: pin reported the 2026-09-10 one and printed a new `fetched` date beside the old filename, bytes, sha256 and row count. cmd_pin now pins the NEWEST snapshot on disk, says `advancing pin: <old> -> <new>`, and takes --snapshot to name one explicitly. Combined with the decode failure, that is how a snapshot reaches 41 days old with nobody having made a mistake.
N2_RETRACTION_WATCH_DECODE.snapshot_age_after: 0 days (pin fetched 2026-10-21, retractionwatch_20261021.csv, 73329 rows, 67729776 bytes, sha256 a2c4d15c45d5931fb994042eaab35448f5d5b9847efce9f06dc0e1efe7474c30); dependency_integrity.py verify prints VERIFIED and 'snapshot age: 0 day(s) since fetch'
N2_RETRACTION_WATCH_DECODE.live_decode_measurement: 19908 of the 73329 lines of the 2026-10-21 snapshot are not valid UTF-8 and were decoded as cp1252. The count is printed by `fetch` as a fact, not an error. Before the fix this snapshot could not be ingested at all.
N2_RETRACTION_WATCH_DECODE.regressions: framework/scripts/test_dependency_integrity.py — ASnapshotThatIsNotUtf8StillBuilds (5 tests: the raw bytes really are undecodable, the rows count and the index builds and RESOLVES to FLAGGED_RETRACTION, the character is recovered not replaced, a valid UTF-8 row is not mangled by the fallback, the pin builds) and ThePinAdvancesToTheNewestSnapshot (2 tests). Full suite 71 tests OK, 2 skipped.
N2_RETRACTION_WATCH_DECODE.mutation_battery_target_updated: M11 pins load_index's source line verbatim and went red when the function lost a `with open(...)` indentation level — the battery working as designed. The target was re-indented and the reason recorded beside it, not the assertion weakened.
N2_RETRACTION_WATCH_DECODE.spend: zero. One key-less public HTTP GET to api.labs.crossref.org, no email address sent, no key, no paid service.
N2_RETRACTION_WATCH_DECODE.third_decoding_site_found_only_after_pin: A bare encoding='utf-8' open of the snapshot lived in test_dependency_integrity.py's own positive control, and it was unreachable until a snapshot that is not valid UTF-8 was pinned: UnicodeDecodeError byte 0x92 at position 6514. The module under test must not be the only place that can read its own data. Routed through snapshot_lines.
N2_RETRACTION_WATCH_DECODE.my_own_test_was_green_for_the_wrong_reas: read_pin took path=PIN_PATH as a DEFAULT ARGUMENT, evaluated once at definition time, so the two new pin tests that redirect dependency_integrity.PIN_PATH at a fixture were silently reading the repository's REAL pin. They passed only because the real pin happened to name the same snapshot the fixture calls 'old', and went red the moment the real pin advanced. Fixed in the module (PIN_PATH resolved at call time) and a third test now asserts the premise directly, because a test green for the wrong reason is worse than a red one. paper_pmids and claim_paper_links carry the same pattern against read-only registries and were deliberately left alone: nothing redirects them, and a change nobody needs is a change nobody tested.
N2_RETRACTION_WATCH_DECODE.upstream_dataset_change_the_stale_pin_wa: Advancing the pin turned the existing positive control red on a real premise change, not a defect: 218 blank-RetractionNature rows in the 2026-09-10 snapshot, ZERO in 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-21, verified with an independent reader over all three files. Retraction Watch classified that whole class between those dates. The 2026-10-02 snapshot had been on disk since the day it was fetched and could not be pinned, so the test went on asserting 218 against a September file for 19 days: the stuck pin was also hiding a real dataset change from the test that exists to notice it. The assertion was rewritten against its PURPOSE — the unclassified branch is unreachable, and zero blank rows is a stronger form of that, not a failure — and the guard that must never pass silently (a blank-nature row WITH a DOI) is unchanged and still 0.

N3_DISMISSAL_LEDGER_D_NUMBERS.result: DONE for the repair an append can honestly make; the other two repairs are named and NOT made
N3_DISMISSAL_LEDGER_D_NUMBERS.what_happened_established_by_measurement: `git log -S'| **D-nn** |'` over dismissal_ledger_current.md returns ZERO commits for every id from D-27 to D-36. No queued work will produce them: the candidates are closed.
N3_DISMISSAL_LEDGER_D_NUMBERS.census_wider_than_the_brief: The brief named four. The live-surface census finds that D-27 through D-36 are ALL cited and none exists, 134 citations repository-wide with D-30 alone cited 52 times. Scoped to surfaces a reader consults as CURRENT — excluding dated records, which correctly cite what they themselves proposed — the unresolvable set is exactly the brief's four: D-31 (discovery_ledger_current.md twice, full_text_queue_current.md), D-33 and D-35 (discovery_ledger_current.md), D-36 (full_text_queue_current.md). N3_DISMISSAL_LEDGER_D_NUMBERS.repair_made: An append-only dated ALLOCATOR ADDENDUM below the DEFAULTS THAT BIT US table. It adds, removes and renumbers no row. It records the measurement, maps every id from D-17 and D-27 to D-36 to its state and to the row it was minted as where there is one, names the candidate each formulation lives in, and tells a reader to read D-31/D-33/D-35/D-36 as citations to a PROPOSED rule and not to a row. It deliberately does NOT reproduce their wording: reproducing a detection rule there is how a row gets minted by accident.
N3_DISMISSAL_LEDGER_D_NUMBERS.repairs_not_made_and_why: Minting the four rows is a BATCH_COMMIT act performed by the integrator from a commit candidate — the table is this ledger's canonical content. Repairing the four citations in place is also a BATCH_COMMIT act, on two research current files. Harness Engineering can append provenance and nothing more, so it appended and stopped, as the brief directed. Recorded rather than fixed — the same disposition the head note's own N6 finding took on 2026-09-28, and the same the integrator stated in BATCH_20260927_004: 'the ledger is append-only; a correction row is the repair'.
N3_DISMISSAL_LEDGER_D_NUMBERS.allocator_hazard_already_closed: The table's maximum id is now D-38, so the head note's max(D-nn)+1 returns D-39 and can no longer collide with a live reference. What remained was purely the dangling-citation defect, which is why no row was minted in haste.
N3_DISMISSAL_LEDGER_D_NUMBERS.ratchet: scripts/test_detection_rule_citations_resolve.py — 6 tests. It parses the table and the addendum, asserts every alias points at a row that exists, that no id is both minted and declared never minted, that every declared never-minted id is actually cited (so the baseline cannot be inflated with bookkeeping about nothing), and holds the unresolved set at zero-beyond-declared with the declared debt bounded at four. Red the moment a fifth non-existent rule is cited from a live surface; it tightens by itself when a BATCH_COMMIT mints one, with nothing to update in the test. It is a ratchet, not a gate: under a second, reports, waits on nobody, and will ask the same informative question at the thousandth batch. The baseline lives in the ledger's own addendum, not in the test, so the constraint is maintained where the content is.
N3_DISMISSAL_LEDGER_D_NUMBERS.scoping_defect_found_by_running_it: The first cut counted the ledger's own allocator prose and reported D-27, D-28, D-29 and the D-39 in the sentence explaining that max+1 now returns D-39 — four findings about its own text, which is how a check teaches a reader to ignore it. The register does not cite itself and is now excluded.
